newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set third consecutive record close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set third consecutive record close.

text.p: French stocks shrugged off news of stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs growth to set a third consecutive closing record on Friday.

The jobs data, which could lead the U.S. Federal Reserve to nudge U.S. interest rates higher, briefly unsettled the market, but French stocks recovered from their lows to push higher. U.S. stocks also advanced.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 9.36 points, or 0.35 percent, at 2,708.28. It hit a historic intraday high of 2,718.95. The futures contract closed up three points at 2,707.
Certain traders said the share markets were starting to look overbought.

"Technically, the European markets are at extraordinary levels. There's an almost unhealthy appetite for risk," said Merrill Lynch strategist David Bowers. He added that investors were beginning to switch into more volatile shares, signalling a deterioration in the quality of the rally.
* Accor rose 3.77 percent to 825 francs on a strong buy recommendation from Morgan Stanley, which put the stock on its "fresh money buy" list.
* Promodes shares rose 6.69 percent to 1,899 francs after reporting a 22 percent rise in net attributable profit to 1.25 billlion francs.

* Broadcaster Canal Plus gained 1.9 percent to 1,074 francs after British Sky Broadcasting Plc and the Kirch group dropped plans to launch the DF1 German digital television service which would have split the German market. Canal Plus is teamed up with Bertelsmann for the Premiere service.
* Pechiney fell 4.44 percent to 258 francs after reporting a net loss of 2.98 billion francs, higher than some forecasts.
